Recurring Payment — Edit

The Recurring Payment form is used to set up payments that repeat automatically.

Recurring payments are useful for regular expenses like rent, utilities, or subscriptions.

This form contains the following fields:

Next issue date

The date when the next payment will be automatically created. This date advances automatically based on your frequency settings.

Set this to match your payment due dates. For example, if rent is due on the 1st, set the next issue date to the 1st.

Interval

The frequency interval for creating payments. This number works with the period type to match your payment schedule.

Common examples: 1 Month = monthly payments, 2 Weeks = fortnightly wages, 3 Months = quarterly fees, 1 Year = annual subscriptions.

PeriodType

The period type that works with the interval to determine frequency. Select the unit of time for your payment cycle.

Choose the option that matches how often you make this payment. Most regular payments are monthly.

MonthDay

For monthly recurring payments, specify which day of the month the payment should be created.

Match this to your actual payment dates. For example, if rent is always due on the 1st, select '1st day of month'.

ExpirationType

Determines when the recurring schedule ends. This controls how long the system will continue creating payments.

Choose 'Until further notice' for indefinite payments like rent, or 'Until date' for loan repayments with a fixed end date.

UntilDate

The date when recurring payments will stop being created. The system will not create any payments after this date.

Use this for loan repayments, fixed-term leases, or any payment series with a known end date.

Paid from

The bank or cash account from which the payment will be made. This account will be credited (reduced) for each payment.

Select the account you typically use for this type of payment. The currency of this account determines the payment currency.

Cleared

The clearing status for bank transactions. Controls whether payments appear as pending or cleared in bank reconciliation.

Use 'Pending' if you want to review and clear payments manually, or 'Cleared' if they should immediately show as reconciled.

Payee

The type of payee receiving the payment. This determines which contact list to select from.

Choose Customer for refunds or credits, Supplier for most business payments, or Other for payments to non-business contacts.

Customer

Select the customer receiving the payment. This links the payment to their account for tracking.

Customer payments might include refunds, overpayment returns, or commission payments to customer-agents.

Supplier

Select the supplier receiving the payment. This links the payment to their account for tracking.

Most recurring payments will be to suppliers for regular business expenses.

Contact

Enter the name of the payee when they're not in your customer or supplier lists.

Use this for one-off payees or personal payments. Consider adding regular payees as suppliers for better tracking.

Description

A description that identifies this recurring payment and will be copied to each generated payment.

Be specific to help with record-keeping. Examples: 'Monthly office rent', 'Fortnightly payroll', 'Quarterly insurance premium'.

Lines

The payment lines specifying which accounts to debit and the amounts. These lines will be copied to each generated payment.

Add a line for each expense category or account affected by this payment. The total of all lines equals the payment amount.

If amounts vary, you'll need to edit individual payments after they're created or update this template.

Automatic reference

When enabled, the system automatically assigns sequential reference numbers to each generated payment.

Recommended for maintaining a clear audit trail. You can still add payment details in the description field.
